subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class bounded memory write API in memory-core, and if so what are the permanent add/replace/remove/list, hard-limit, duplicate, and secret-safety semantics?
rationale: The request creates public tool, config, persistence, and security behavior that cannot be chosen safely from source inspection alone.

options.title: Define bounded memory CRUD
options.body: Use this issue to settle the memory-core write contract, then implement the chosen API and security policy in focused slices.

options.title: Limit scope to flush bounds
options.body: Treat existing and proposed append-only flush guards as sufficient for now and leave manual Markdown memory edits as the supported write path.

options.title: Defer built-in writes
options.body: Decline first-class memory writes until plugin and memory-role direction is clearer, keeping docs and current recall tools as the supported surface.

recommendation.title: Define bounded memory CRUD
recommendation.body: Use this issue to settle the memory-core write contract, then implement the chosen API and security policy in focused slices.

likelyOwner.reason: The memory-core, memory flush, plugin-boundary, and config history points most strongly to steipete as the best available routing owner for the product/API decision.
